conventions.node_type_in_json: Lowercase registry key ("domain", "socialaccount"), as Flowsint stores nodeType and as native exports emit it. PascalCase class names ("Domain") are used in GraphQL and Markdown. Lookup is case-insensitive in Flowsint.
conventions.node_id: Import-local id = <key>:<canonical identity>. The identity comes from the type's identity selector and canonicalizers (identity-config-v1). Composite selectors join values with '|'. Values longer than 96 characters, values with tabs, newlines, or other control characters, and identity values of sensitivity class secret, financial, or government_id use <key>:h:<first 16 hex of sha256(canonical)>. Never reuse one id for two different entities.
conventions.node_label: The Flowsint compute_label() result. emit.py computes it with the real Pydantic model when a Flowsint interpreter is available; otherwise it falls back to the UI label_key, then the primary field.
conventions.properties: Only fields of the Flowsint type, with their declared names. Flowsint types accept extra keys (extra=allow); emit.py keeps unknown keys and reports them. Never use reserved property names.
conventions.relationship_label: UPPER_SNAKE_CASE verb phrase, read source -> target. Use a label from the relationship catalog. Prefer a native label when its definition fits. Use an extension label only when no native label fits. IS_RELATED_TO is the last resort and needs a caption that states the nature of the link.
conventions.relationship_direction: Emit one direction only. Never emit a relationship and its inverse. For symmetric labels, order the endpoints by id.
conventions.relationship_properties: Native edge properties are date, caption, type, weight, confidence_level. Put fact qualifiers (role, start_date, end_date, amount, currency) in properties as well; keep evidence in extensions.
conventions.nested_vs_edge: Flowsint types can embed other types (Whois.domain, Individual.email_addresses). When an embedded entity matters to the investigation, also emit it as its own node and connect it with the matching relationship, as the enrichers do.
conventions.one_fact_one_edge: Each relationship is one claim that can be true or false. Split compound sentences into several edges. Time-bound facts carry date or start_date/end_date.
conventions.uncertain_identity: Two mentions that may denote the same entity are two nodes linked by POSSIBLY_SAME_AS with evidence. Never merge on a guess. Merge only when the canonical identity is equal.

evidence_model.where: Node and relationship evidence lives in extensions["flowsint-ontology.evidence"] = {version: 1, data: {confidence, status, evidence: [...]}}. A short summary goes in node.metadata (extraction_id, confidence, sources) and in relationship.properties.confidence_level. The source catalog lives in the top-level extensions["flowsint-ontology.extraction"].

evidence_item.source: Id of a source in the source catalog (S1, S2, ...). Required.
evidence_item.locator: Where in the source: URL fragment, page and paragraph, line, timestamp, message id. Required when the source has more than one part.
evidence_item.quote: Verbatim excerpt that supports the claim, at most 300 characters. Redact secrets.
evidence_item.observed_at: ISO 8601 date or datetime at which the fact was true or observed, if known.

methods.stated: The source asserts the fact in words (a document, a person in a conversation, a profile field).
methods.observed: The agent or a tool saw the fact directly in technical data (DNS answer, HTTP response, file hash).
methods.inferred: The agent concluded the fact from other facts. State the reasoning in the quote or in a gap note. Cap confidence at 0.7 unless a second independent source confirms.
methods.enriched: A Flowsint enricher or an external tool produced the fact. Name the tool in locator.
methods.derived: The fact follows mechanically from another value (email domain part -> Domain, URL host -> Domain). Confidence follows the parent value.

source_reliability.A: Completely reliable: authoritative registry, official record, direct technical observation.
source_reliability.B: Usually reliable: established outlet, reputable vendor report, verified account.
source_reliability.C: Fairly reliable: generally accurate source with occasional errors.
source_reliability.D: Not usually reliable: anonymous blog, unverified account, scraped aggregator.
source_reliability.E: Unreliable: known for errors, deception, or fabrication.
source_reliability.F: Reliability cannot be judged: new or unknown source.

confirmed: Two or more independent reliable sources, or direct technical observation.
probable: One reliable source, consistent with other facts.
possible: One weak source, or an inference from reliable facts.
doubtful: Weak, contradicted, or single unreliable source.
refuted: Evidence shows the claim is false. Keep only when the refutation matters.

evidence_model.combining: Node or edge confidence = 1 - product(1 - c_i) over independent evidence items, capped at 0.99; dependent items (same origin) count once. emit.py applies this when a node or edge has no explicit confidence.

special_category.basis: GDPR art. 9 and art. 10 (racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious beliefs, health, genetic and biometric data, criminal convictions and offences).
special_category.rule: Record only when the input states it explicitly and the investigative purpose requires it. Never infer it. emit.py lists every such value in the Markdown report.

government_id.basis: National identifiers (passport, ID card, SSN, tax id, driving licence, voter id).
government_id.rule: Record only when stated in the input and required by the purpose. Never guess a format or complete a partial number.

financial.basis: Account numbers, card numbers, balances, income, credit data.
financial.rule: Record when stated and required. Keep the value exact because it is an identity field; the report masks it to the last 4 characters.

secret.basis: Live authentication material: passwords, CVV, session tokens, API keys, private keys, seed phrases.
secret.rule: Never record plaintext. Passwords: keep only a hash the source provides; never hash a plaintext password yourself (weak passwords are reversible); otherwise omit it and list it in excluded. High-entropy tokens and keys: store sha256:<hex> or a masked form (****1234). Node ids for secret identity values are hashed. emit.py blocks values that look like plaintext secrets.

asn_as_form.algorithm: Trim a string, remove one case-insensitive leading AS prefix, parse the remaining ASCII decimal digits as a non-negative integer, and emit AS followed by the base-10 integer without leading zeroes. Other forms block.

cidr_network.algorithm: Parse with Python ipaddress.ip_network semantics using strict=false and emit the compressed network address plus prefix length. Invalid values block.

credit_card_digits.algorithm: Trim and remove non-ASCII-digit separators, retaining only 0-9. An empty result or any non-separator letter blocks. Validation such as Luhn is separate from identity canonicalization.

crypto_address.algorithm: Apply exact_string first. If the result matches 0x followed by exactly 40 hexadecimal digits, lowercase the complete Ethereum address. Preserve every other cryptocurrency address exactly because case may be meaningful.
crypto_address.case_rule: lowercase Ethereum only; preserve all other address case

dns_value.algorithm: Apply ip_compressed for exact record_type A or AAAA; apply domain_idna for exact record_type CNAME, NS, or PTR; otherwise apply exact_string. MX and SRV values remain exact because presentation formats vary and no parser contract is frozen.

domain_idna.algorithm: Apply Unicode NFC and trim, remove one trailing root dot, encode each label as an IDNA2008 A-label under RFC 5890/5891, and lowercase the result. Empty, malformed, or non-domain values block.

email_address.algorithm: Apply Unicode NFC and trim, require exactly one valid addr-spec boundary, preserve the local part byte-for-character, and canonicalize the domain with domain_idna. Invalid values block.
email_address.case_rule: preserve local-part case; lowercase IDNA domain

ethereum_address.algorithm: Apply exact_string, require 0x followed by exactly 40 hexadecimal digits, and lowercase the complete value. Invalid values block.

exact_integer.algorithm: Require a JSON integer and emit its base-10 representation without leading zeroes. Strings, floats, booleans, arrays, objects, and null block.

exact_string.algorithm: Normalize with Unicode NFC and trim leading and trailing Unicode whitespace. Preserve all internal characters and case. Non-string values block.

hash_lower.algorithm: Apply exact_string and lowercase the result. Hash syntax and length validation remain field-specific validation concerns.

individual_name.algorithm: Normalize with Unicode NFC, trim, and collapse each run of Unicode whitespace to one ASCII space. Preserve letter case. Non-string and empty results block.

ip_compressed.algorithm: Parse as an IPv4 or IPv6 address with standards-based IP parsing and emit its compressed canonical form. Invalid values block.

phone_e164.algorithm: Parse and validate with libphonenumber semantics, requiring an international country code unless a field-specific region is supplied by a future contract, then emit E.164. Ambiguous national numbers block.

url_standard.algorithm: Apply Unicode NFC and trim, parse an absolute URL under RFC 3986, lowercase the scheme, canonicalize the host with domain_idna and lowercase it, remove the default port for the scheme, and preserve userinfo, non-default port, path, query, and fragment character case. Parse failures block.
url_standard.case_rule: lowercase scheme and host; preserve path/query/fragment case

username.algorithm: Apply Unicode NFC and trim, remove exactly one leading @ when present, and preserve the remaining characters and case. Empty results block.
username.case_rule: case-sensitive after one leading @ is removed

fields.name: associated_phones
fields.title: Associated phones
fields.description: Phone numbers associated with the account

Technology.name: Technology
Technology.description: Represents a technology, framework, or software detected during recon.

identity.notes: Version is not part of the registered primary identity.

extraction_hints.recognize: Software, framework, or product a site or host uses.
extraction_hints.identity_tip: name; version as property.

fields.name: source
fields.title: Source
fields.description: Tool or method that detected the technology (e.g. httpx)

Username.name: Username
Username.description: Represents a username or handle on any platform.

identity.case_rule: case-sensitive after one leading @ is removed
identity.notes: Platform remains a property; SocialAccount supplies the platform-aware composite identity.

extraction_hints.recognize: A handle without a confirmed platform account ("@jdoe", "jdoe92").
extraction_hints.identity_tip: value without the leading @; platform as property.
extraction_hints.avoid: When the platform and profile are known, also create SocialAccount and link Username -HAS_SOCIAL_ACCOUNT-> SocialAccount.

fields.name: last_seen
fields.title: Last seen at
fields.description: Last time this username was observed

Weapon.name: Weapon
Weapon.description: Represents a weapon with detailed specifications and forensic information.

identity.notes: Serial number is not silently substituted for the registered primary name.

extraction_hints.recognize: A weapon of investigative interest.
extraction_hints.identity_tip: name; serial_number as property.

fields.name: type
fields.title: Category
fields.description: Weapon category (handgun, rifle, shotgun, knife, etc.)

fields.name: modifications
fields.title: Modifications
fields.description: Any modifications made to the weapon

fields.name: firing_mode
fields.title: Firing Mode
fields.description: Firing mode (single shot, burst, full auto, etc.)

WebTracker.name: WebTracker
WebTracker.description: Represents a web tracking technology with privacy and compliance information.

identity.notes: Tracker domain and script URL do not participate.

extraction_hints.recognize: Analytics/ad tracker id (UA-, G-, GTM-, pixel id).
extraction_hints.identity_tip: tracker_id.

Website.name: Website
Website.description: Represents a website with its URL, domain, and redirect information.

identity.notes: Default ports are removed; non-default ports remain.

extraction_hints.recognize: A URL or web page.
extraction_hints.identity_tip: absolute URL with scheme; default port removed.
extraction_hints.avoid: Do not use Website for a bare domain.

fields.name: redirects
fields.title: Redirects
fields.description: List of redirects from the website

Whois.name: Whois

accepted_forms: domain object with a string domain member
blocking_forms: domain object without a string domain member

selector_override.rationale: Refine the primary Domain object to its nested domain scalar for canonical matching.

identity.notes: The nested Domain value is extracted explicitly; arbitrary objects are never stringified.

extraction_hints.recognize: A WHOIS registration record of a domain.
extraction_hints.identity_tip: nested domain.domain.

fields.name: city
fields.title: City
fields.description: City where the domain is registered

fields.name: country
fields.title: Country
fields.description: Country where the domain is registered

fields.name: creation_date
fields.title: Creation Date
fields.description: Date when the domain was created

relationships.label: AFFILIATION_WITH
relationships.definition: The reified Affiliation is with the target organisation.

relationships.label: ANNOUNCES
relationships.definition: The autonomous system originates the IP prefix in BGP.

relationships.label: ASSOCIATED_WITH_DEVICE
relationships.definition: The selector was found on, or used from, the device (infostealer logs). Native use: e-mail, phone, username.

relationships.label: ASSOCIATE_OF
relationships.definition: The actors have a social or business association that no more precise label covers (partner, co-founder, co-defendant, frequent contact).

relationships.label: AUTHORED
relationships.definition: The actor or account wrote or created the content.

relationships.label: BELONGS_TO
relationships.definition: The IP, prefix, or organisation belongs to the autonomous system (routing or operator relation).

relationships.label: BELONGS_TO_DOMAIN
relationships.definition: The website's host is the domain.

relationships.label: CERTIFICATE_COVERS
relationships.definition: The certificate names the domain in its subject CN or SAN.

relationships.label: COMMUNICATES_WITH
relationships.definition: The malware, device, or host makes network contact with the target (C2, beacon, exfiltration endpoint).

relationships.label: CONNECTION_WITH
relationships.definition: A breach or intelligence record links the selector to the person. Weak association, not proof of ownership.
relationships.notes: Native in the dehashed and intelligence enrichers. Prefer HAS_EMAIL / HAS_PHONE / HAS_USERNAME (person as source) when a source states that the person uses the selector.

relationships.label: CONTAINS
relationships.definition: The source contains the target: prefix contains address or sub-prefix; archive or document contains a file. Native use: CIDR contains IP.

relationships.label: CONTROLS
relationships.definition: The actor operates or administers the target without proven ownership (account operator, infrastructure administrator, nominee arrangement).

relationships.label: DISTRIBUTED_VIA
relationships.definition: The malware or file is distributed through the website, domain, message, or account.

relationships.label: DROPS
relationships.definition: The malware or script writes or downloads the file, script, or second-stage malware.

relationships.label: FOUND_IN_BREACH
relationships.definition: The selector appears in the catalogued breach.

relationships.label: FOUND_IN_LEAK
relationships.definition: The selector or artefact appears in the leak or dump.

relationships.label: HAS_ADDRESS
relationships.definition: The organisation's registered or head-office address.

relationships.label: HAS_AFFILIATION
relationships.definition: The person holds the reified Affiliation (role with its own dates and evidence).

relationships.label: HAS_ALIAS
relationships.definition: The source is also known by the alias.

relationships.label: HAS_ATTACHMENT
relationships.definition: The message carries the file or document.

relationships.label: HAS_CERTIFICATE
relationships.definition: The host presents the X.509 certificate.

relationships.label: HAS_CREDENTIAL
relationships.definition: The selector or actor has the login credential.

relationships.label: HAS_DNS_RECORD
relationships.definition: The domain has the DNS resource record.

relationships.label: HAS_DOMAIN
relationships.definition: The source is bound to the domain: registrant organisation, e-mail domain part, or website host.

relationships.label: HAS_EMAIL
relationships.definition: The source uses, publishes, or is reachable at the e-mail address.

relationships.label: HAS_GRAVATAR
relationships.definition: The e-mail address has the Gravatar profile.

relationships.label: HAS_INNER_TEXT
relationships.definition: The website's visible text contains the phrase.

relationships.label: HAS_LEADER
relationships.definition: The organisation has the person as director, officer, executive, or legal representative.

relationships.label: HAS_PHONE
relationships.definition: The source uses, publishes, or is reachable at the phone number.

relationships.label: HAS_PORT
relationships.definition: The IP exposes the port (open, filtered, or observed).

relationships.label: HAS_REGISTERED_DOMAIN
relationships.definition: The actor or e-mail appears as registrant of the domain (reverse WHOIS).

relationships.label: HAS_RELATED_DOMAIN
relationships.definition: The domains share registrant data or history (reverse WHOIS, historical records).
relationships.notes: Direction from the investigated domain to the discovered domain.

relationships.label: HAS_REPUTATION
relationships.definition: The entity has the reputation score from a provider.

relationships.label: HAS_RISK_PROFILE
relationships.definition: The entity is assessed by the risk profile. Native use: IP fraud score.

relationships.label: HAS_SCRIPT
relationships.definition: The website loads or embeds the script.

relationships.label: HAS_SESSION
relationships.definition: The credential or account opened the session.

relationships.label: HAS_SOCIAL_ACCOUNT
relationships.definition: The handle (or actor) has the account on a platform.

relationships.label: HAS_SUBDOMAIN
relationships.definition: The parent domain has the child hostname.

relationships.label: HAS_TRACKER
relationships.definition: The website embeds the tracker id.

relationships.label: HAS_USERNAME
relationships.definition: The source uses or exposes the handle. Native use: the local part of an e-mail as a candidate handle.

relationships.label: HAS_WEBSITE
relationships.definition: The domain serves the website.

relationships.label: HAS_WHOIS
relationships.definition: The domain has the WHOIS registration record.

relationships.label: HELD_AT
relationships.definition: The account or card is held at the financial institution.

relationships.label: HOSTED_IN
relationships.definition: The domain's addresses are announced by the autonomous system.

relationships.label: HOSTS
relationships.definition: The IP serves the domain or website (passive DNS, reverse-IP, virtual hosting).

relationships.label: INFECTED
relationships.definition: The malware infected the device.

relationships.label: ISSUED_BY
relationships.definition: The certificate or card was issued by the organisation (CA, card issuer).

relationships.label: IS_ADMINISTRATIVE_CONTACT
relationships.definition: The actor is the administrative contact of the domain in WHOIS.

relationships.label: IS_BILLING_CONTACT
relationships.definition: The actor is the billing contact of the domain in WHOIS.

relationships.label: IS_REGISTRANT_CONTACT
relationships.definition: The actor is the registrant contact of the domain in WHOIS.

relationships.label: IS_RELATED_TO
relationships.definition: Generic link whose nature no catalogued label expresses. Flowsint default label.
relationships.notes: Last resort. Requires a caption that states the nature of the link; emit.py rejects it without one.

evidence.anomaly: Upstream typo (digit zero) in the test-only domain_to_dummy enricher.
evidence.note: item is Domain or Email (dummy data).

relationships.label: IS_SUBDOMAIN
relationships.definition: Native direction (website_to_subdomains): the parent website -> a website served on one of its subdomains.
relationships.notes: The label reads backwards; keep the native direction. For Domain -> Domain use HAS_SUBDOMAIN.

relationships.label: IS_TECHNICAL_CONTACT
relationships.definition: The actor is the technical contact of the domain in WHOIS.

relationships.label: LINKS_TO
relationships.definition: The source contains a hyperlink to the target.

relationships.label: LIVES_AT
relationships.definition: The person resides or resided at the place.

relationships.label: LOCATED_AT
relationships.definition: The source is physically at the place (establishment, server geolocation, device position, item found). Native use: organisation establishment.
relationships.notes: For a person, use LIVES_AT for residence and LOCATED_AT with a date for presence at a time.

relationships.label: MEMBER_OF
relationships.definition: The actor belongs to a group, association, party, board, or network, without an employment relation.

relationships.label: MENTIONS
relationships.definition: The content names or refers to the entity without asserting a stronger relation.
relationships.notes: Use it to link a relevant source document to the entities it reports; use the specific label for the fact itself.

relationships.label: ORIGINATED_FROM
relationships.definition: The session, message, or connection came from the IP or device.

relationships.label: OWNS
relationships.definition: The source legally or beneficially owns the target. Native use: wallet owns NFT.
relationships.notes: For operational control without proven ownership use CONTROLS.

relationships.label: POINTS_TO
relationships.definition: The DNS record's value designates the target (A/AAAA -> Ip; CNAME/NS/MX/PTR -> Domain).

relationships.label: POSSIBLY_SAME_AS
relationships.definition: Identity hypothesis: the two nodes may denote the same real-world entity. Both nodes stay separate until a human decides.
relationships.notes: Both endpoints must have the same type. confidence_level states the strength of the hypothesis; evidence states the matching features.

relationships.label: PUBLISHED_ON
relationships.definition: The content was published at the website or account.

relationships.label: REGISTERED_BY
relationships.definition: The WHOIS record names the target as registrant contact.

relationships.label: REGISTERED_IN
relationships.definition: The domain's registrant is located at the place, according to WHOIS.

relationships.label: RELATIVE_OF
relationships.definition: The persons are family members. Put the kind of kinship in properties.type (spouse, parent, sibling, child, ...); for directed kinship order source as the elder or the parent.

relationships.label: REPLY_TO
relationships.definition: The message replies to the earlier message.

relationships.label: RESOLVES_TO
relationships.definition: DNS A/AAAA resolution of the domain returns the IP.

relationships.label: REVERSE_RESOLVES_TO
relationships.definition: The IP's PTR record names the domain.
relationships.notes: Not a strict inverse of RESOLVES_TO: PTR and A records are independent. Emit the one actually observed.

relationships.label: SAMPLE_OF
relationships.definition: The file or script is a sample of the malware family.

relationships.label: SENT
relationships.definition: The sender (account, address, number, or actor) sent the message.

relationships.label: SENT_TO
relationships.definition: The message was addressed to the recipient.
relationships.notes: properties.type = to | cc | bcc | dm | group.

relationships.label: SENT_TRANSACTION
relationships.definition: The wallet is the sender of the reified transaction node.

relationships.label: SUBSIDIARY_OF
relationships.definition: The organisation is owned or controlled by the target organisation (subsidiary, branch, front).

relationships.label: TLS_INFO
relationships.definition: A TLS handshake on the domain produced the HTTPS website node that carries the certificate details (domain_to_tls).
relationships.notes: Native only. For new certificate facts use HAS_CERTIFICATE -> SSLCertificate.

relationships.label: TRANSACTION
relationships.definition: On-chain transfer from the source wallet to the target wallet. Native: created by cryptowallet_to_transactions via create_wallet_transactions, merged on hash.
relationships.notes: Put the transaction hash in properties.hash: Flowsint merges TRANSACTION edges on it.

relationships.label: TRANSACTION_TO
relationships.definition: The reified transaction pays the target wallet.

relationships.label: TRANSFERRED_TO
relationships.definition: Off-chain value transfer (wire, card payment, cash) from the source to the target.
relationships.notes: For on-chain transfers between wallets use the native TRANSACTION.

relationships.label: USES_MALWARE
relationships.definition: The actor deploys or operates the malware.

relationships.label: USES_TECHNOLOGY
relationships.definition: The website or host runs the technology.

relationships.label: WORKS_FOR
relationships.definition: The person is employed by, or works on behalf of, the target (organisation, or the person that WHOIS lists as the main contact).

evidence.anomaly: Upstream emits Individual -WORKS_FOR-> Email. Semantically wrong: use Individual -HAS_EMAIL-> Email.

relationship_calls.label: IS_RELATED_TO
relationship_calls.note: item is Domain or Email (dummy data).
relationship_calls.anomaly: Upstream typo (digit zero) in the test-only domain_to_dummy enricher.

relationship_calls.label: WORKS_FOR
relationship_calls.anomaly: Upstream emits Individual -WORKS_FOR-> Email. Semantically wrong: use Individual -HAS_EMAIL-> Email.
